sections.content:
Population change in Rossendale in 2032

The population in Rossendale is projected to increase from 71,187 people in 2022 to 73,090 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 3,006 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Rossendale
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Rossendale, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 1,524, with 6,591 births and 8,115 deaths in Rossendale between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in Rossendale by 2.1%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 3,006, with 39,428 people moving to the area and 36,422 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Rossendale by 4.2%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 578, with 860 people moving to the area and 1,438 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Rossendale by 0.8%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 936, with 1,718 people moving to the area and 782 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Rossendale by 1.3%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Rossendale in 2032

The median age in Rossendale is projected to rise from 42 years in 2022 to 43 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 21% of the population in Rossendale are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 18% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Rossendale between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Rossendale is projected to stay the same, at around 63%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 293 to 302 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Rossendale?

In 2032, 20% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 23% in 2022.

This is the same as the average for England in 2032.

Looking at the youngest age groups in Rossendale between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
